text: I am ready to begin the examination of the newborn presenting with respiratory distress. Please provide the patient's gestational age, birth weight, and any relevant maternal history or symptoms observed at birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is a 33-week preterm presenting with early respiratory distress, which is highly suggestive of Hyaline Membrane Disease (Respiratory Distress Syndrome) due to surfactant deficiency. To confirm this clinical suspicion and rule out other causes like pneumonia or congenital heart defects, I need to visualize the lung fields. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of fine reticular granulation and ground glass appearance are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease) in a premature infant. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease)
